items.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: I’m going to do Doris Day, Rosie Clooney and Jo Stafford... I guess it was Jo Stafford got what I’ve got today, kind of a laryngitis thing and couldn’t sing. I lost her.

ctx.x: Sounds like whoever did “I Left My Heart in San Francisco” must have heard that recording.

Yeah, they copied it from that, yeah. And then yeah, that was used again in that. And anyway, and then I did the Marty Robbins stuff, “White Sport Coat.” So Mitch — you asked about the deal. Mitch said, at a meeting, he said, “hey everything this Conniff guy’s doing is getting on the charts,” you know. And so he was going out to the west coast, and he said, “I won’t be using you for a couple of weeks, I’m going out to the west coast, and I’m going to do Doris Day, Rosie Clooney and Jo Stafford.” And I said, “Oh,…

anyway, so we did the Rosie sessions, and you asked — I still didn’t answer the question about the deal. So anyway when we got back — oh Mitch says I’m going to make it up to you when we get back, when we get back to New York. So that’s what he did. He gave me that single that I told you about, “Begin the Beguine” and “Stardust.” And that was the way he would wheel and deal, which developed into the album.
